domestic.debt_note: Total public debt Rs81.4tn as of early FY26 (per capita debt ~Rs325,000); debt-to-GDP 70.7% at end-FY25 (64.3% on FRDLA netted basis); finance advisor says public debt growth eased to ~5% in FY26 vs prior years (https://profit.pakistantoday.com.pk/2026/04/03/pakistans-per-capita-debt-rises-to-rs325000-as-total-public-debt-reaches-rs81-4-trillion/, https://www.brecorder.com/news/40427429/pakistans-public-debt-growth-eases-to-5-in-fy26-says-finance-advisor)
domestic.remittances: FY26 full-year remittances $41.6bn, +8.6% YoY; June 2026 alone $3.475-3.5bn (+2% YoY, -18.3% MoM) as SBP incentive schemes wound down (https://www.brecorder.com/news/40429234/overseas-pakistanis-send-416bn-in-fy26-as-sbp-ends-incentive-schemes, https://www.samaa.tv/2087353274-overseas-pakistanis-send-3-5bn-in-remittances-in-june-sbp)
domestic.current_account: Jul-May FY26 (11-month) current account surplus of $255mn; SBP Governor guiding toward a balanced-to-surplus full FY26 outturn on remittances/services exports outpacing import growth; June/full-year FY26 print not yet released (https://www.arabnews.pk/node/2647503/pakistan, https://www.brecorder.com/news/40429111)

global_read: Global tape is mixed-to-nervous, not clean risk-on: S&P/Dow still up modestly (+0.42%/+0.29% 1d) but VIX jumped +9.1% 1d to 16.39 and Brent spiked +3.6% 1d to $78.73 on Mideast conflict risk (per georisk.json), a combination that argues for caution on PSX despite a stable PKR (277.77, +0.03% 1d) and soft DXY.
drivers: SBP held policy rate at 11.5% at the final FY26 MPC review on 2026-06-15, citing inflation on track to the 5-7% medium-term target and reserves rising to $17.2bn as of June 5 post IMF reviews (https://www.thenews.pk/story/1420738-sbp-maintains-115-policy-rate-in-final-fy26-review)

Next MPC decision (first of FY27) is 2026-07-27; SBP also announced a full FY27 MPC calendar with quarterly press conferences for transparency (https://propakistani.pk/2026/06/23/sbp-to-announce-first-monetary-policy-decision-of-fy27-on-july-27/, https://www.brecorder.com/news/40427077/sbp-announces-fy27-mpc-meetings-schedule)

CPI eased to 11.1% YoY in June 2026 from 11.7% in May (-0.3% MoM); core NFNE urban inflation also decelerated to 8.7% from 9.0% — disinflation trend intact but still double-digit (https://www.brecorder.com/news/40428026/pakistan-inflation-hits-111-in-june-2026, https://www.brecorder.com/news/40428129/june-cpi-inflation-up-111pc-yoy)

IMF Executive Board completed 3rd EFF review / 2nd RSF review on 2026-05-08, unlocking ~$1.32bn (~$1.1bn EFF + ~$220mn RSF); program assessed on track with GDP growth, contained inflation and reserve rebuilding ahead of program projections (https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/05/08/pr-26147-pakistan-imf-completes-3rd-rev-of-extended-arrangement-under-eff-and-2nd-rev-arrang-rsf)

SBP-held FX reserves rose sharply to $18.47bn as of 2026-07-03 (+$1.94bn w/w on GoP inflows), total liquid reserves (incl. banks) $23.99bn; this was despite ~$9bn in external debt repayments in Q4 FY26 (https://www.thenews.pk/print/1424970-sbp-forex-reserves-rise-1-9bn-to-18-47bn-as-of-july-3)

Latest T-bill auction (2026-07-08, settled 2026-07-09): 6M cut-off 11.4375%, 12M 11.4880%, both easing vs prior auction — money market pricing in gradual, not aggressive, further easing (https://mettisglobal.news/SBP-raises-over-Rs2tr-through-MTBs-auction-61694)

Latest PIB auction (2026-07-02, settled 2026-07-06): 10-year cut-off eased 47bp to 12.14% from 12.61% at the prior auction — long end pricing in continued disinflation (https://mettisglobal.news/SBP-raises-Rs615bn-in-Fixed-Rate-PIB-Auction-61543)

FY26 remittances hit a record $41.6bn (+8.6% YoY); June alone $3.475-3.5bn, still solid support for the external account even as SBP unwinds special incentive schemes (https://www.brecorder.com/news/40429234/overseas-pakistanis-send-416bn-in-fy26-as-sbp-ends-incentive-schemes)
Current account tracking toward balance/slight surplus for FY26 (11-month Jul-May surplus of $255mn); full FY26 and June prints not yet released by SBP (https://www.arabnews.pk/node/2647503/pakistan)

Georisk radar (state/georisk.json) reads 47/100 'moderate' — driven by conflict/escalation stress (US-Iran strikes, domestic petrol/diesel price hikes of Rs13+/litre passed through on 2026-07-11) and USD/oil-driven stress; this argues against upgrading to risk-on even though domestic anchors (reserves, CPI trend, IMF) are constructive

Regime held at NEUTRAL: domestic fundamentals continue to improve (reserves +$1.94bn w/w, CPI decelerating, record remittances, IMF disbursed and on track, T-bill/PIB yields easing) but a same-day VIX spike (+9.1%) and Brent spike (+3.6%) tied to Mideast conflict risk, plus event risk from the 2026-07-27 MPC, keep the desk from calling risk-on
